findings.title: Light theme color regression in .topic-meta-data h5 a
findings.body: Original: `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);`. Changed to: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));`. The PR's stated goal is to add dark-theme support without altering light theme rendering, but here the light-theme branch now uses 70% lightness instead of 30%, producing a markedly lighter text in light mode (visual regression). The dark-theme branch is also wrong: with the original light value of 30% (a darker shade), the symmetric dark-theme value should be `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)`, not 30%, so dark mode will render the text too dim against a dark background.

findings.title: Light theme color regression in .custom-message-length
findings.body: Original: `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%);`. Changed to: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%));`. The light-theme branch was changed from 70% to 30%, the inverse of the original. Compared with the desktop counterpart (`desktop/modal.scss` line 94) which correctly preserves 70% for the primary branch and uses 30% for secondary, this file has the values swapped: in light mode the text will now be much darker than before, and in dark mode it will be much lighter than intended.

findings.title: Light theme color regression in .topic-map h3
findings.body: Original: `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%);`. Changed to: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`. The light-theme value was changed from 20% to 50%, making the heading noticeably lighter in light mode. The matching desktop file (`desktop/topic-post.scss` line 321) keeps 20% for primary and uses 80% for secondary, which is the correct pattern. The dark-theme value is also wrong here (should be 80% to keep prominence on a dark background, not 50%).

findings.title: Light theme color regression in .group-member-info .name
findings.body: Original: `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);`. Changed to: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`. The light-theme value was changed from 30% to 50%, making the name text lighter in light mode. The dark-theme value should be 70% (to mirror the original 30% prominence on a dark background) but is 50%. The matching `.title` rule one block below correctly uses 50%/50% symmetric values because its original was already 50%.

findings.title: Light theme color regression in .group-member-info .name
findings.body: Original: `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);`. Changed to: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`. The light-theme value was changed from 30% to 50%, lightening the name text in light mode. The dark-theme value should be 70% (mirroring the original 30% prominence on dark backgrounds) but is 50%. This is inconsistent with the sibling `.title` rule directly below, which correctly uses 50%/50% because its original lightness was already 50%.

findings.title: Light theme color regression in .group-member-info .name
findings.body: Original: `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);`. Changed to: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`. The light-theme value was changed from 30% to 50%, lightening the name text. The dark-theme value should be 70% to maintain similar prominence on a dark background, but is 50%. Same pattern as the parallel bugs in desktop/user.scss line 522 and mobile/topic-post.scss line 497.
